$comment: Pixel coordinates read off the reference photographs, in each photograph's own
pixel space at the committed resolution. This file is the hand-read input;
tools/model/measure.py converts it to millimetres in dimensions.json. A read is
changed here and the converter re-run, never typed into dimensions.json.
Methods: 'profile' = numeric detection from a colour/brightness mask along a row
or column; 'eye' = read off a gridded copy of the photograph at 4000 px, so
about +/-10 px; 'fit' = least-squares fit to detected boundary points.

board.shows: the back shell open, board component side up, tube face up, front shell removed

camera.$comment: Leica Q2, fixed 28 mm lens, full frame; the committed file is the full frame downscaled from 8368 px.

scale_bar.$comment: TMS1370 DIP pin pitch. 20 pins a side counted on board-L1001567.jpg (20 dark peaks across the pin row there). Pitch by autocorrelation of the pin-row profile: 41.6 px on L1001567, 22.6 px on L1001568. Pin pitch on a DIP is 2.54 mm.

front.shows: the assembled unit from the front, powered, near plan view

scale_bar.$comment: No object of known size in frame; scaled from the shell width derived on the board photograph.

shell.$comment: Outer edge of the back shell's rim (the mating face). x from the red mask; the wing and module edges from the per-column red profile.

rim_above_board_mm.$comment: Estimate, used only for the perspective correction: the rim is nearer the camera than the board by about this much. Bounded from the photograph itself: the board's right edge (pcb.x[1]) reads 7 px inside the shell's outer edge, and a board plane 15 mm below the rim would have moved it 70 px inward, so the two planes are within a few mm of each other in this frame. Bound +/-5 mm.

tube.$comment: shroud = the black end caps and frame; glass = the clear envelope between them; face = the printed segment area inside the glass.

pcb.$comment: The brown phenolic board. outline: corners clockwise from top-left, read off the overlay; the bottom edge steps down for the central tongue and the right end. The left end is hidden under the battery box.

battery_box.$comment: Abuts the shell's left wall; the left read is the wall's inner face.

lever_disc.$comment: The grey disc with a steel pin through it, under the launcher lever's well. Its pin is the lever the player moves.

discretes.$comment: Small parts read by eye off the gridded board photograph as [x0, y0, x1, y1] boxes, with what each is where the silkscreen says. The toothed black disc beside the 1815/2120 labels is not identified.

electrolytics.$comment: Radial electrolytic capacitors lying on the board, as [x0, y0, x1, y1] of the can.

colours.$comment: Pixel boxes on assets/reference/case/front.jpg (4032 x 3024) where each material shows its colour; measure.py samples them. The red is taken from the lit part of the module face above the window, the blues from the fire cap's crown and the sticker, black from the switch thumb. Read off the rectified texture and converted back to the photograph's pixels (0.0949 mm/px, case corner at 261, module top at 716).

white_reference.$comment: The sticker: its white print is the brightest thing in the box.

svg.$comment: The flat page's case drawing, src/ui/geometry.ts and src/ui/case.ts, in its 896 x 440 viewBox units, for the cross-check the PRD asks for. Copied with citation, not imported.

shell.$comment: left is under the owner's finger; read where the wing's top edge meets the finger's shadow, +/-15 px.

bands.$comment: Left to right across the face: the raised stippled block of each wing, the smooth inboard strip each wing carries, and the module. Read off crops of the photograph at 1.5x.

scope.$comment: Circle first fitted to the dark window's boundary, then corrected by eye against the overlay (the fit pulls low because the lit tube breaks the top boundary); rectangle edges from a 2x crop.
